text.p: State-controlled telecommunications firm PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia (Telkom) is discussing the possibility of setting up multimedia services with other firms, the Jakarta Post newspaper said on Wednesday.
The paper quoted Telkom president Asman Akhir Nasution as saying company hoped to extend its range of services into the multimedia business that in order to keep up with competition.
This would include offering video and news services on demand to subscribers, initially in the Jakarta area, the daily said.
"However, we have not planned any joint multimedia company. The process will take a long time," Nasution was quoted as saying.
Telkom officials were unavailable for comment on Wednesday.

The newspaper said Nasution met President Suharto's son Bambang Trihatmodjo of the Bimantara Group, Peter Sondakh of the Rajawali Group and Rali Siregar of private television station RCTI, a unit of Bimantara Citra PT, to discuss the issue.
